title: Every segmented control is the one system glass morph, everywhere
goal: User 2026-09-29, with a screenshot of the history bar's All / Screenshots / Videos filter showing a solid blue thumb: 'I'm seeing inconsistent segmented controls. What I'd like to see is the system glass morph consistently.' The shared SegmentedControl has a .accent plate style used by HistoryOverlay.swift:113 (solid blue), a .raised glass style elsewhere, and a hand-rolled motion; try-the-segmented-thumb-on-the-system-s-own-liqu adds the system morph behind a flag. The user has decided: the system glass morph is the only one.
acceptance: The system glass morph (from try-the-segmented-thumb-on-the-system-s-own-liqu) is the only way any segmented control draws and moves: its temporary flag is removed, the hand-rolled TimelineView motion and SegmentThumbMorph are deleted (drag keeps only what it needs), and there is no plate style choice (.accent and .raised variants removed)

The history bar's filter, the title bar's View | Edit, and every panel picker look and move identically (same rail, same glass thumb, same selected label treatment), differing only in size classes the design system defines

An inventory of every segmented or tab-like control in Sources/Photonz (grep SegmentedControl, Picker .segmented, NSSegmentedControl, and hand-built button rows acting as one) is in the task log, each confirmed on the shared control
comp-segmented.html and UX-PATTERNS say there is one segmented control and one style
A test fails if a plate style parameter or any other segmented implementation reappears
Filmed with filmThumb in three places (history bar, title bar, a panel): same motion, never outside the rail; photographs of all three side by side
